grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle the Factory cards, randomly select players + 1 face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: select number of players + 1 Factory cards; one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories; choose one structure bonus tile. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: Place each character at its home base; place two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; place four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; put six stars by the faction emblem; put six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with black squares; structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; recruits in the bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement. Starting power and combat-card draw come from the Faction Mat. Starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards come from the Player Mat.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup pieces table and step 3: Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and objectives.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. If both actions are taken, top must precede bottom; top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before acting, then take as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired; the Player Mat and upgrades determine the costs and benefits.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: may take either, both, or neither but must move token; bottom first is not allowed; pay full cost, then choose as much or as little benefit.
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you keep the abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone controls it and resources; enemy units do not gain your structure abilities; spend resources from any currently controlled territories.
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No. A normal Move can move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. All units can pick up, carry and drop any number of resources. Only mechs can carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker's transport does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: move up to two different units; cannot use both selections to move same unit twice. All units carry resources; only mechs carry workers; carried movement does not count as worker's own movement.
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Having too little or zero popularity does not stop their retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers, and workers cannot independently enter or leave territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move rules: entering enemy workers only causes immediate retreat and one popularity lost per worker, down to zero; workers cannot independently enter or move into/out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve combats before the following bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: after all units finish a Move action, fights occur before any subsequent bottom action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Move rules restrict workers entering or leaving enemy character/mech-controlled territory alone.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gains either two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gains either any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card; empty deck reshuffle rule. Trade: pay $1, choose two resources or one popularity; resources placed on controlled territory containing a worker; cannot trade for resources if all workers at home.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full, including power, popularity and/or coins, before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers never return to the Player Mat, and exposing new costs changes only future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce: pay every exposed cost in full before production; each worker in selected territories produces; take new workers from Player Mat left to right after payment; may decline; new costs affect future actions.
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; it moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake, and its newly uncovered ability applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Costs vary with the mat and upgrades. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Upgrade and Deploy: pay exposed mat costs in oil/metal; stated effects and placement restrictions. Bottom-row actions: may still pay after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits.
grades.reason: Oil/metal resource costs, bracketed cube restrictions, worker/control/lake deployment and ability scope, completed-action payment resolved; no universal numerical cost was requested.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total can occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives its bonus production only while you control its territory; an enemy there can remove your control, so the Mill cannot produce then. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your unit movement even while an enemy occupies its territory. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: placement, one structure limit, no lakes/home bases, structures cannot be moved or destroyed. Mill only while controlled; Mine remains a personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Put the recruit token from any bottom-row section into any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat permanently, and immediately gain that chosen space's two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle exposed where you removed the recruit. When you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom action, resolve the active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor, stopping if a sixth star ends play. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: permanent placement and one-time choices; circle uncovered determines ongoing bonus; active player then left then right; two-player opponent once.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly chooses dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. Reveal simultaneously, total dial plus card values, and attacker wins ties. If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first and defender second. Both deduct their selected dial power from their Power Track and discard played cards face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–4: simultaneous secret dial selection, optional cards per character/mech, People's Army extra card, simultaneous reveal and tie rule, abilities order, and payment.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources. Losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat (including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake); a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's combat exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one, and with two places none; Saxony places a star after each victory while it has star tokens. You may keep fighting at the limit. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 5–6: control, retreat/resources, combat stars, popularity loss and losing-card reward.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; if contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token remains. Only a character triggers it. Put all gained resources, workers, mechs, and structures on the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action cost, and receive no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: only character triggers; after Move and all combats; token stays if contested entry lost; gains go to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat bonuses.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player's character must choose one available Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if necessary; this is not just the first player to visit. Each player gets one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. It acts as a fifth section with optional top then bottom, subject to the normal no-repeat rule except Rusviet. Similar Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom Move action moves one unit up to two territories within that action, or up to three for a character/mech with Speed, subject to Mine access and normal stop restrictions.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: every character picks on first finish of Move there; one permanent card; fifth section; no mat/recruit/building bonuses; bottom Move distance and Speed.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: You may reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal; you may wait to reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the objective deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, all requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom, Saxony exception.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars normally), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars cannot be lost, and another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists every star goal, permanence, no blocking, and sixth-star ending.
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve recruit bonuses active player first, then left, then right, checking for a sixth star after each; if one ends the game, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end: bottom action collection order, neighbor recruit sequence, and pending-battle movement rollback.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete resource pair. Five stars add $20. Four normal controlled territories plus the Factory count as seven, adding $21. Thirteen resources make six complete pairs, adding $12; total added to held coins is $53. Add the selected structure bonus from your structures even if enemies control their territories. Victory goes by total coins, then workers + mechs + structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune: popularity 7–12 rates; Factory is three counts; complete pairs rounded down; structures qualify despite enemy control; listed tiebreakers.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.

grades.question: Is a home base a territory, may you enter one normally, and are expansion home bases active?
grades.expected_answer: Home base is not territory for any game effect; cannot normally move back in, build/deploy there. Starts and forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare explicit movement exception. Two unrepresented bases are expansion placeholders/inactive.
grades.observed_answer: A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: home base is not a territory; entry exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders.
grades.reason: Non-territory home base/default prohibitions, explicit exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders resolved.

grades.question: Which terrain produces each token, do Factory/lake produce, are workers resources, and what happens if resource supply runs out?
grades.expected_answer: Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village workers. Lake/Factory nothing. Workers not resources. Resource supply unlimited; use multipliers as necessary, no territory token/unit limit.
grades.observed_answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if necessary.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce terrain table; resources paragraph says workers are not resources and resource tokens have no supply limit.
grades.reason: All terrain outputs/no-output spaces, nonresource workers, unlimited resources and territory quantities resolved.

grades.question: May resources be picked up/dropped mid-movement, can mechs carry characters, and what does unlocked Speed change about tunnels and stops?
grades.expected_answer: All units may pick/drop any resources; mechs also own workers, never character. Speed adds one territory for character/mechs, including before/after tunnel jump which costs one move; may pick/drop mid-move. Entering enemy unit ends movement/cannot move again turn; character encounter also stops.
grades.observed_answer: Any unit can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; only mechs can carry your workers, and never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, so the added step can be before or after it. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: all units carry resources, mechs carry workers; Speed and tunnel jump step rules; stops override Speed.
grades.reason: All-unit resource pickup/drop, mech own-worker/no-character carriage, Speed/tunnel step and overriding stops resolved.

grades.question: Can workers capture a territory controlled only by an enemy structure, and are printed tunnels usable by all unit types?
grades.expected_answer: Yes any unit may enter structure-only territory and controls it; no combat from structure alone. All printed tunnel territories adjacent for Move by any unit; enemy Mine not a public tunnel.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Any unit may enter territory held only by an enemy structure and take control without combat. Printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Move rules: entry into enemy-structure-only territory; all printed tunnels adjacent for any unit.
grades.reason: Any unit captures enemy structure-only territory, no structure combat, all-unit printed tunnels versus personal Mine resolved.

grades.question: If unable to afford any action after last using Move, must you pay a partial Produce cost or what turn is legal?
grades.expected_answer: Never partial payment; full cost required. Take a dead turn choosing another section with no actions, still moving token.
grades.observed_answer: You may not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. The token must move from the section used last turn, so after using Move you choose a different section.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: pay costs in full, never part; if unable to afford any action, move token to a different section and take neither.
grades.reason: Full payment required; legal dead turn shifts token and takes neither action resolved.

grades.question: What do Armory and Monument grant, when do those benefits trigger, and can an enemy occupant take them away?
grades.expected_answer: Armory adds 1 power when owner takes Trade, Monument adds 1 popularity when owner takes Bolster. Uncovered benefits apply future respective top actions, regardless territory control; opponent never gains them. Factory similar actions excluded.
grades.observed_answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are future matching top-action bonuses from the uncovered structure benefits. You keep your structure abilities even without control of the territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
grades.reader_evidence: Build structure effects; control rules say abilities remain without control except Mill production, and enemy units do not gain abilities.
grades.reason: Trade Armory power/Bolster Monument popularity, future triggering and owner persistence versus enemy control resolved.

grades.question: How does each base faction Riverwalk differ, which units receive it, and does Nordic Swim give lake movement or help its mechs?
grades.expected_answer: Riverwalk only character/mechs: Saxony and Nordic forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic faction Swim workers only across rivers to any land terrain, never lakes; no mech/character benefit.
grades.observed_answer: Riverwalk destinations for character/mechs are Rusviet: farms and villages; Crimea: farms and tundra; Nordic: forests and mountains; Polania: villages and mountains; Saxony: forests and mountains. These destinations apply to character/mechs. Nordic Swim lets workers cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs or mechs generally.
grades.reader_evidence: Faction table identifies Riverwalk destinations; Nordic Swim description says workers alone, not lakes, and no help to character/mechs.
grades.reason: All five Riverwalk terrain pairs/character-mech scope and worker-only Nordic river/not-lake Swim resolved.

grades.question: Which locations become adjacent under Saxony Underpass and Rusviet Township, and which units can use those shortcuts?
grades.expected_answer: Underpass controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mechs. Township controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mechs. Not workers; required ability unlocked via deploy.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
grades.reader_evidence: Unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township explicitly specify character/mech Move actions.
grades.reason: Saxony controlled mountains+tunnels and Rusviet controlled villages+Factory, character/mech-only adjacency resolved.

grades.question: When does Saxony Disarm apply, how often, and how does Nordic Artillery differ?
grades.expected_answer: Disarm before combat on printed tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power once per combat, not per unit. Artillery before any combat may pay 1 power to make opponent lose 2, once per combat. Track losses; attacker ability before defender.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery is different: before combat you may pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery descriptions.
grades.reason: Saxony tunnel/Mine Disarm versus Nordic paid Artillery, timing/track reductions/once-per-combat resolved.

grades.question: With Rusviet People's Army, how many cards may two mechs and three workers play, and can workers alone fight?
grades.expected_answer: Three cards: one per mech plus one total for at least one worker. Need character/mech; workers alone cannot fight. Ability unlocked.
grades.observed_answer: Two mechs and three workers permit three combat cards total: the normal one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total from People's Army when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight; combat still requires a character or mech.
grades.reader_evidence: Rusviet People's Army: two mechs and three workers allow three cards; combat rules require character/mech and workers alone never fight.
grades.reason: Three-card result from two mechs plus worker presence, and character/mech combat requirement resolved.

grades.question: Where may Crimea Wayfare move its character/mechs, and can they enter an active opponent home base?
grades.expected_answer: From territory or home base to own home base or any inactive faction home base regardless distance, including inactive expansion bases. Not active opponent home base; workers do not gain ability.

grades.reason: Wayfare own/inactive bases, any distance/origin and no active-opponent-base/worker exception resolved.

grades.question: What does Crimea Scout steal and when; how does Coercion value and limit a spent combat card?
grades.expected_answer: Scout before combat randomly steals one opponent combat card to hand, once per combat not per unit. Coercion once per turn spends one combat card as any one resource regardless card value; card not worth end-game coins.

grades.reader_evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting Coercion descriptions.
grades.reason: Random precombat Scout steal/once limit, Coercion one card for one arbitrary resource regardless number resolved.

grades.question: How do Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge differ in lake movement and retreat, and what happens to transported workers/resources when leaving a lake?
grades.expected_answer: Both character/mechs to/from lakes, workers only via mech; cannot leave workers/resources behind when carrier leaves; worker cannot leave without mech. Nordic may retreat character/mechs onto adjacent lake (or home), carrying workers; Polania may move lake to any lake, no such special retreat. Both cannot build/deploy lake, can fight another lake-capable faction there.

With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off, and a carrier cannot leave workers or resources behind on a lake. Both allow lake combat; neither permits building or deploying on lakes.
grades.reader_evidence: Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake movement edge-case paragraph.
grades.reason: Lake movement versus Nordic retreat/Polania lake jumps, cargo/worker restrictions and no lake builds/deploy resolved.

grades.question: When does Polania Camaraderie prevent popularity loss, and does it cover driving out undefended workers?
grades.expected_answer: Prevents popularity loss for workers forced to retreat after winning combat as aggressor on own turn. Does not apply to driving out undefended workers without combat; normal one popularity each then.

grades.reason: Camaraderie only combat-winning aggressor/on-own-turn; no undefended-worker displacement exception resolved.

grades.question: How does Polania Meander resolve encounters, including card count, options and paying the second option?
grades.expected_answer: Draw just one card; may choose up to two different options in either order; may use first benefit to pay second cost.
grades.observed_answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. Resolve each option in turn; the first gain may pay the second option's cost. The summary does not say Polania draws or uses two encounter cards; it specifies up to two options on one card.
grades.reader_evidence: Meander: up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.
grades.reason: One card/up to two different options, either order and first gain paying second resolved.

grades.question: If a character reaches an encounter during Factory bottom Move, can it continue moving, and does the encounter occur before all combats finish?
grades.expected_answer: No character movement again that turn; Factory Move obeys stop rules. Encounter after entire Move and all combats; character must remain there. Bottom Factory Move still triggers normal encounter.

Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; the encounter does not happen before combats finish.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounter rules say character stops; after whole Move action and all combats; same rules apply during Factory Move.
grades.reason: Factory Move encounter stop and after-all-combats timing resolved.

grades.question: What information about coins, combat cards and objectives is public, and is the exact coin total required on request?
grades.expected_answer: Coin holdings not hidden but need not reveal total value; combat card count public, contents secret; may conceal whether cards used in combat until reveal. Objectives secret until revealed.
grades.observed_answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, though during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents remain secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
grades.reader_evidence: Public and hidden information table.
grades.reason: Coin information/optional total disclosure, combat count versus contents/commitment concealment and objective secrecy resolved.

grades.question: Which things can be exchanged in alliances, are agreements enforceable, and can a payment cancel combat once begun?
grades.expected_answer: Only tangible exchange coins (tournament exception no coin trades for deals/alliances); informal agreements unenforceable. Cannot cancel already initiated combat by negotiation; must fight after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.
grades.observed_answer: Informal agreements are unenforceable, and coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (with coin deal/alliances forbidden in tournament play). Negotiation cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat must be fought after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements section states exchange, enforceability and initiated combat rules.
grades.reason: Only coin exchanges/tournament exception, unenforceable agreements and mandatory initiated combat resolved.

grades.question: State all final-scoring popularity tiers and payouts; do controlled lakes and home bases count, and do leftover single resources score?
grades.expected_answer: 0-6: stars3/territories2/pairs1;7-12:4/3/2;13-18:5/4/3. Lakes count if controlled, home bases never. Factory three total. Sum controlled resources across board and score floor(total/2), no leftover single; workers not resources.

Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a single leftover resource scores nothing.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune popularity table and territory/resource counting paragraphs.
grades.reason: All three scoring tiers/rates, lakes/home/Factory, pooled floor pairs/no workers resolved.

grades.question: For adjacent-tunnel, adjacent-encounter and adjacent-lake structure bonuses, how are duplicates, rivers, removed encounters and Mines treated, and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: Count each qualifying adjacent feature once across structures. Rivers do not break adjacency; removed encounter tokens still count printed encounter. Mine not tunnel for tile. Adjacent tunnels count1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6=$9; lakes/encounters1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6-7=$9; zero=$0.
grades.observed_answer: For adjacent-feature tiles, count unique printed tunnel territories (not Mines), unique lakes, or unique printed encounter locations (even when tokens have been removed); count each feature once across all structures. The summary does not specify a special exception for duplicate adjacency beyond uniqueness. Rivers do not break adjacency. For 1 feature pay $2; 2–3 pay $4; 4–5 pay $6; tunnels pay $9 at 6, while lakes and encounters pay $9 at 6–7. Zero scores $0.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table gives qualifying unique features and payout bands; rivers do not break adjacency.
grades.reason: Three adjacency tile features/unique counting/rivers/removed encounter/Mine exception and exact payout ranges resolved.

grades.question: For structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras, what qualifies and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: On printed tunnels not Mine:1=$2,2=$4,3-4=$6. Longest continuous straight line only, rivers do not break:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Farms+tundras combined number with structures:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Zero=$0. Bonus regardless territory control.
grades.observed_answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6. For structures in a row, count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9. For structures on farms/tundras, count combined qualifying structures; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus table rows for structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras.
grades.reason: Printed-tunnel versus Mine, longest continuous straight row/rivers, combined farm+tundra and each exact payout resolved.

grades.question: In combat on a lake, does a winning attacker lose popularity for workers carried by the defeated mech?
grades.expected_answer: Yes one popularity per forced-retreat worker even carried on lake; retreat with mech to home base by default (Nordic Seaworthy permits adjacent-lake retreat). Polania unlocked Camaraderie exception after combat.

grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 6 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
grades.reason: Winning lake attacker loses popularity for carried defeated workers, normal retreat and named faction exceptions resolved.

grades.question: Does placing a popularity star protect current popularity or its scoring tier, and can two factions both star the same achievement?
grades.expected_answer: Star itself permanent, popularity may fall and final payout uses current tier. Other factions may also place same goal; no blocking.
grades.observed_answer: Placing a popularity star is permanent, but it does not protect current popularity or its final-scoring tier: current popularity at game end determines scoring. Two factions may both place stars for the same achievement because other players' stars never block a goal.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end: stars permanent even if popularity later drops; current popularity determines final scoring; other players' stars never block a goal.
grades.reason: Permanent star versus mutable current scoring tier, other factions sharing goal resolved.

grades.question: How are Faction Mats and Player Mats assigned, and in what relative faction order should players sit? Why does that seating matter for recruit bonuses?
grades.expected_answer: Randomly shuffle the Faction Mats and Player Mats and deal one of each to each player. Players sit near their faction home bases, with the clockwise order from the top Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, using the factions in the game. Recruit ongoing bonuses respond to the player and their immediate left/right neighbors, so those neighbors follow the seating arrangement.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONGOING BONUS and PLAYER ORDER
grades.observed_answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seat order matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can be triggered by the active player and immediate left/right neighbors, in active-then-left-then-right order.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: random mats and faction seating order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left/right neighbors trigger and sequence.
grades.reason: Random mat assignment, complete prescribed clockwise faction order and immediate-neighbor recruit consequence resolved.

grades.question: For movement, what distinguishes a river from a lake, and from which surrounding land territories can a unit with a lake-movement ability enter the lake?
grades.expected_answer: A river lies on the border between two land territories. A lake comprises an entire territory hex and extends from that hex to any adjacent shoreline. A unit with the appropriate lake-movement ability can move onto it from any of the surrounding territories shown by that shoreline; crossing permission for a river alone does not grant entry to lakes.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES; RIVER; LAKE; illustrated example
grades.observed_answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
grades.reader_evidence: Move rules define river and lake; lake-capable unit entry from any surrounding adjoining land territory.
grades.reason: River as land border, lake as entire hex extending to adjacent shores, lake-ability entry and river-only insufficiency resolved.

grades.question: When you draw an encounter card, may you keep it private? What must you show or read aloud to the other players?
grades.expected_answer: The encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud, then read through its costs and benefits and choose an option. The rules do not require reading every option aloud.

grades.reader_evidence: Encounter procedure: show card to all players, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text; options need not all be read.
grades.reason: Encounter card/art public and capitalized thematic text read aloud resolved; reading every option aloud is not required.

grades.question: Is there any limit to the number of your units or resource tokens that may occupy one territory?
grades.expected_answer: There is no per-territory limit on same-faction units or resource tokens. This does not remove the separate one-structure-per-territory restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p11 NO LIMIT: no limit to same-faction units on a territory
Rulebook PDF p13 NO LIMIT: any number of resource tokens or workers can be on a territory

grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
grades.reason: No per-territory limit on same-faction units or resource tokens resolved; separate structure limit remains.

grades.question: Must the next player wait until the current player has finished every bottom-row decision, or when may the next turn begin?
grades.expected_answer: The next clockwise player may begin when the current player starts or is finalizing a bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin while current player decides which bottom-row item to gain after starting a noninteractive bottom-row action.
grades.reason: Next clockwise player may begin while noninteractive bottom-action decision is underway; priority/end restrictions retained.

grades.question: After taking the selected top-row or bottom-row action, may you pay its cost again to take that same action a second time in the same turn?

grades.question: What can you gain from the normal, unupgraded Move action if you choose not to move any units?

grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.
grades.reason: Normal Move coin alternative gives $1 instead of movement resolved.

grades.question: May a worker already on the board be returned to your Player Mat to cover a Produce cost again, including after it retreats?

grades.reason: Workers never return to Player Mat/cover Produce costs; retreat destination remains home base resolved.

grades.question: May you initiate combat when you have zero power, zero popularity, or both?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Neither power nor popularity has a minimum requirement for initiating combat. You can select zero power on the dial.

grades.observed_answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat section: you may attack with zero power/popularity.
grades.reason: Zero power, zero popularity or both do not bar combat initiation resolved.

grades.expected_answer: Yes. The limit restricts further combat stars, not participation or winning. It may continue fighting but gains no additional combat-victory stars.

grades.reason: Ordinary two-combat-star cap limits further stars, not future combats or winning resolved.

grades.question: For a faction without Meander, may you decline to choose an option after drawing an encounter, choose an option you cannot afford, or decline some of the chosen option benefits?

grades.reason: Non-Meander encounter requires one affordable option/full printed cost, but benefits may be partly or wholly declined resolved.

grades.expected_answer: They select dial power simultaneously and secretly, then reveal both Power Dials and any selected combat cards simultaneously. Attacker-first resolution of combat mech abilities does not make the power selection or reveal sequential.

grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose, then reveal simultaneously.

grades.question: When taking a bottom-row action, what must you announce to the other players, and why?

grades.reason: Mandatory bottom-action announcement lets immediate neighbors check ongoing recruits resolved.

grades.question: After you achieve a star goal, may you decline or delay placing that star to avoid ending the game? How does this differ from holding a completed objective card unrevealed?
grades.expected_answer: An earned star must be placed on the appropriate achievement immediately; it cannot be declined or delayed to avoid ending the game. You may instead wait to reveal a completed objective, provided you still satisfy it when you reveal it; when you reveal it, place the star.

Rulebook PDF p2 TRIUMPH TRACK: as soon as you complete a requirement
Rulebook PDF p26 OBJECTIVES: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal
grades.observed_answer: No. A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved; because the sixth star immediately ends play, you cannot delay or decline a star to avoid ending the game. An objective differs because you may wait to reveal a completed objective, but must meet all its requirements at the moment you reveal it.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved; sixth star ends immediately. Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal.
grades.reason: Earned threshold star placement mandatory/immediate; completed objective reveal may wait while requirements hold resolved.

grades.question: Before any faction or mech ability provides an exception, may a character, mech or worker move across a river or onto a lake?
grades.expected_answer: No. By default, none of the three unit types may cross rivers or move onto lakes. An applicable special ability is required to override the relevant restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 5: TYPES OF UNITS: all three unit types can move around the board, not over rivers or onto lakes by default.
Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES: By default, units may not move across rivers or onto lakes; some mech abilities break the rule.
grades.observed_answer: Normally, no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions; Nordic Swim allows only workers to cross rivers to land terrain and not lakes.
grades.reader_evidence: Move rules: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities are exceptions.
grades.reason: All three unit types face default river/lake movement prohibition absent applicable ability resolved.

grades.question: After placing an enlisted recruit on a Recruit One-Time Bonus space on your Faction Mat, may you move that recruit token later to free the space for another recruit?

grades.expected_answer: No. Only characters trigger encounters. A mech or worker entering a territory does not resolve its encounter or remove the encounter token; it remains for a character.

Rulebook PDF p.31, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters may have encounters.

grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

grades.question: While you control the territory containing your Mill, how does it affect the number of territories you may Produce on and the output there, including when no actual worker is present?

The Mill counts as one producing worker itself, even with no actual worker there; each actual worker at the Mill also produces normally, so Mill output is added rather than substituted.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce Mill paragraph specifies extra territory, Mill's own output, actual workers' additional output, and allowance examples.
grades.reason: Controlled Mill adds bonus production territory, produces as one worker without actual worker, and actual workers may also produce resolved.

grades.question: What presence establishes control of a territory, and do resources alone preserve your control after your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure?

source_references: Rulebook PDF p4, CONTROL: control requires at least one unit or a structure with no enemy units; only one player controls a territory at a time.
Rulebook PDF p4, RESOURCES: resource tokens remain on the board and may be spent only from territories currently controlled.
Rulebook PDF p29, EVERY TERRITORY CONTROLLED and EVERY 2 RESOURCES CONTROLLED; PDF p31, END-GAME SCORING.
grades.observed_answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control it.
grades.reader_evidence: Control definition: unit present, or your structure there with no enemy unit.
grades.reason: Control needs unit or own structure without enemy units; resources alone do not maintain control/spending after last unit leaves resolved.

grades.question: Which resource is used to pay for the Build action, and which is used to pay for the Enlist action?

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?

On mats: four mechs over faction abilities, six stars by faction emblem, six cubes in black-square green boxes, four structures in matching boxes, four recruits in bottom-row circles, remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles, and action token beside Player Mat ready for first placement; one-time recruit spaces stay empty. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup steps 3–4.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.

Rusviet may repeat a section, but top and bottom actions each remain once per turn. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: different section; full cost; optional benefit; Rusviet limit.
